course.name: FlowScript
course.description: Read and edit a board as FlowScript, then verify its compiled graph and output.
course.longDescription: Prerequisite: Thinking in Flows. Use Desktop or web with the FlowScript workspace and standard catalog. In 25 minutes, create a text normalizer from source, change one expression, and recover from a compiler diagnostic. Checks are manual; applying source and running the graph are separate steps.

lessons.title: Read the text form of a graph

challenges.prompt: A call requires message. Should you replace that key with the UI label Message?
challenges.explanation: FlowScript arguments use catalog input pin names and their declared casing.

options.label: No; use the exact declared input pin name
Yes; display labels are always source identifiers
Only if the node is on the left

challenges.prompt: Source compiled without diagnostics. What remains before calling the normalizer verified?
challenges.explanation: Compilation checks the source and graph contract; execution checks the required outcome.

options.label: Assume compilation proved the intended message
Apply/review the graph and run its event against the expected output

lessons.title: Use declarations to repair an error

challenges.prompt: Compilation reports that string::trim has no matching call shape for text. What is the targeted repair?
challenges.explanation: The declaration specifies string as the input key. A compiler diagnostic should lead to a precise source correction.

options.label: Look up the declaration and restore the string argument key

challenges.prompt: A reusable function needs branch-dependent output. What shape fits its return rules?
challenges.explanation: Value-returning functions require a single final return outside control blocks.

options.label: Assign a local result in the branches and return once afterward

lessons.title: Make a source change and verify it

challenges.prompt: You are changing one existing logger’s Message. What should happen to its generated node anchor?
challenges.explanation: Generated anchors connect source statements to existing graph identities.

options.label: Remove it to force a fresh ID
Copy another node’s anchor over it
Keep it so the edit targets the existing node

challenges.prompt: A new node has two data outputs and an unfamiliar argument shape. Where should you establish the call contract?
challenges.explanation: The current declaration supplies the actual input keys, types, and named outputs.

options.label: Its current catalog declaration and compiler diagnostics
A guessed JavaScript API with a similar name
